messages:
emily (PM): kicking off a PRD + acceptance criteria review for the routing + fallback policy. goal: clear launch scopes and tradeoffs by EOD.
sanjay: linked a quick doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd-routing-fallback (wip)
lina: added high-level goals in the doc: 1) latency SLOs 2) cost containment 3) functional compatibility across model variants
matt: can we list the customer-driven asks up front? primary asks: deterministic fallbacks, region pinning, and drift detection during rollouts
rachel: +1 on drift detection. also need audit log entries for every automatic fallback decision (customer audits will ask)
kevin: ops question: should fallbacks be synchronous (blocking) or async (queue + eventually serve)? tradeoffs: latency vs user visible errors
emily (PM): proposal in doc: two phased launch
emily (PM): Phase 1 (MVP): deterministic tiered routing, region-aware routing, simple model-compatibility whitelist, exhaustive logging for decisions. No automated retraining or ML-based routing.
emily (PM): Phase 2: policy optimizer + heuristics for latency/cost tradeoffs and canary-based automatic variant promotion
lina: MVP acceptance criteria (draft):
- latency: 95th <= policy SLO per-tier (configurable)
- fallback correctness: fallbacks only to compatible variants as defined in model-compat matrix
- observability: every decision emits trace + fallback_reason tag
- safety: customer data does not leave pinned region unless explicitly opted in
matt: edge cases to add:
- tokenization incompatibility between variants (e.g., opt vs llamap) -> fallback should prefer variants with same tokenizer family
- function-calling schema mismatch -> reject fallback and surface error to app
rachel: add: KV cache presence mismatch (hot prefix present on primary but not on fallback) -> flag as degraded but allow fallback if latency SLO at top-tier
kevin: infra constraints: some regions have only quantized variants. policy must be able to mark region-tier incompatibilities and fall back to cross-region only when allowed by customer config
emily (PM): suggested acceptance test list (automated):
- simulate capacity loss in region A, verify routing to region B if cross-region fallback enabled
- intentionally create model variant failure (OOM) and ensure deterministic fallback chosen
- run synthetic workload and validate cost delta within expected bounds
sanjay: sample policy YAML I dropped into the doc for discussion:
```
policy:
  tiers:
    - name: low-latency
      sLO_ms: 200
      allowed_variants: [gptx-8k-fp16, gptx-8k-8bit]
    - name: cost-saver
      sLO_ms: 500
      allowed_variants: [gptx-8k-8bit, gptq-16k]
  region_policies:
    eu-west-1:
      prefer_local: true
      cross_region_fallback: false
    us-east-1:
      prefer_local: true
      cross_region_fallback: true
  compatibility_matrix:
    gptx-8k-fp16: [gptx-8k-8bit, gptq-16k]
```
lina: that looks good. can we add a compatibility tag for tokenizer and function-calling schema? e.g. tokenizer_family: "byte-fusion". then policy can prefer same-family variants
matt: acceptance criteria addition: rollout safety gates
- canary: <1% traffic for 1 hour, monitor perplexity + latency
- auto-rollback if quality regression > 5% or latency 95th > configured SLO
rachel: for launch scope negotiation: Customer-driven asks we will defer to phase 2 unless it's low-effort: per-customer region pinning is medium effort (ops + infra), prefer to ship templated region policies first and offer per-customer override as enterprise feature
kevin: infra notes: need an admin API for emergency overrides (manual route pins) and visibility into active fallbacks. that must be part of MVP
emily (PM): launch criteria (MVP):
- policy engine + config UI + admin override API
- policy rules enforced in serving runtime with telemetry + logs
- basic compatibility matrix support and tokenization tagging
- documented behavior for the 5 most common edge cases
- QA signoff on the three automated tests above
sanjay: question on billing: do we bill by primary selection or actual serving variant? affects customer expectations for dedicated and reserved capacity
emily (PM): billing doc: bill based on actual serving variant to be transparent. call out in release notes
matt: one more edge case: user-provided prompt that uses model-specific special tokens -> fallback should run pre-check and either transform or reject with explicit error
rachel: UX for app devs: include header in response: `X-Redwood-Fallback: <variant>` and `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: <code>` so they can instrument behavior
kevin: logs need unique IDs for each fallback decision to tie traces -> `fallback_id` in logs
emily (PM): next steps: lina + matt to update PRD with tokenizer compatibility fields and rollout gates by EOD. kevin to spec admin API. sanjay to update billing section. rachel to draft the five edge-case doc entries.
lina: noted, will add tokenizer_family and function_schema tags. will propose a small compatibility JSON schema.
matt: will write the canary test harness and add automated rollback in the deployment pipeline
rachel: will do edge-case doc and a short FAQ for customers
kevin: I’ll sketch admin API endpoints: POST /admin/overrides, GET /admin/fallbacks
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging-policy-engine v0.3 -> Tue 10:30 UTC
emily (PM): thanks everyone. if we can get updates by EOD we can cut a beta next week. :rocket:
kevin: :thumbsup:
lina: :eyes:
matt: will do
